title: Connecting an AI agent
snippet:
Give your agent an API key, and it can request and fund a virtual card on your behalf using USDG or ETH on Robinhood Chain.
## 1 Get your API key
[Sign in](/) to get one.
## 2 Connect it to Claude Desktop
Claude Desktop supports remote MCP servers on every plan, including free, with no special setup needed. Here is how to add Paygent.
1. Open Claude Desktop and go to **Settings**
2. Find **Connectors** (sometimes labeled MCP) and choose **Add custom connector**
3. Set the **Name** to `Paygent`
4. Set the **Remote MCP server URL** to your MCP URL with your API key appended as a query parameter, since some clients do not offer a separate header field:
```
https://mcp.paygent.tech/sse?api_key=pgt_live_your_api_key_here
```
5. Leave the OAuth fields blank, then click **Add**
6. Start a new chat, confirm **Paygent** is enabled for that conversation (look for a tools icon near the message box), and just ask naturally. For example: *"Use Paygent to create a card for me."*
Claude will show you what it is about to do and ask for confirmation before calling any tool that funds or modifies something, so you stay in control at every step.
## 3 Or configure any other MCP client
Most MCP clients, including Claude Code and other agent frameworks, accept a config block like this instead.
```
{ "mcpServers": { "paygent": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.paygent.tech/sse", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer pgt_live_your_api_key_here" } } } }
```

5 Tool reference
| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| create_card | Get a deposit address; a card is issued automatically for whatever arrives |
| card_details | Poll for card status; returns card number, security code, and expiry once funded and active |
| card_balance | Check just the current balance and last four digits, always fresh, no sensitive fields |
| card_transactions | List recent card transactions |
| close_card | Close the card and refund the remaining balance to your wallet |
| deposit_history | View on chain deposit history |
| release_hold | Release any on hold deposits to a given address |
| wallet_balance | Current USDG and ETH wallet balances |
| withdraw_link | Get a link to withdraw wallet balance externally |
| withdrawal_history | Withdrawal history |

## 7 Minimal Node.js client
```
import { Client } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js"; import { SSEClientTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/sse.js"; const API_KEY = process.env.PAYGENT_API_KEY; // never hardcode this async fun

title: @paygent-ai/mcp-server
snippet:
## Paygent MCP Server
Connect **Cursor**, **Claude Desktop**, **VS Code**, and other AI assistants to your Paygent account.
The Paygent MCP server exposes **49 tools** (kept under 50 for Cursor / Antigravity) covering customers, agents, plans, invoices, payments, usage, wallets, orders, quotations, and billable metrics.
**Production API URL:** `https://api.withpaygent.com/api`
---
### Configuration
Credentials can be passed as CLI flags or environment variables:
| Variable | Flag | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PAYGENT_BASE_URL` | `--server-url` | API base URL (production: `https://api.withpaygent.com/api`) |
| `PAYGENT_API_KEY` | `--api-key` | API key from Settings → API Keys (`pk_…`) |
Copy `.env.example` to `.env` for local development. Never commit real keys.
---
#### Quick Start (production)
##### 1. Get your API key
Paygent → **Settings → API Keys** → Create a key (`pk_…`).
##### 2. Add to Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`)
Until `@paygent-ai/mcp-server` is published to npm, run the built local entry (or a path your team distributes):
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"paygent": {
"command": "node",
"args": [
"/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/paygent-mcp-server/dist/index.js",
"start",
"--server-url",
"https://api.withpaygent.com/api",
"--api-key",
"YOUR_PAYGENT_API_KEY"
]
}
}
}
```
After npm publish (see below), replace the `node` + path with:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"paygent": {
"command": "npx",
"args": [
"-y",
"@paygent-ai/mcp-server",
"start",
"--server-url",
"https://api.withpaygent.com/api",
"--api-key",
"YOUR_PAYGENT_API_KEY"
]
}
}
}
```
Save and **reload Cursor** (Command Palette → Developer: Reload Window).
##### 3. Try it
- "List my customers"
- "Show invoice aging"
- "What's my revenue this month?"
---
#### VS Code
```json
{
"servers": {
"paygent": {
"type": "stdio",
"command": "npx",
"args": [
"-y",
"@paygent-ai/mcp-server",
"start",
"--server-url",
"https://api.withpaygent.com/api",
"--api-key",
"YOUR_PAYGENT_API_KEY"
]
}
}
}
```
(Use `node` + `dist/index.js` instead of `npx` until the package is published.)

#### Local development only
```bash
cp .env.example .env   # set PAYGENT_API_KEY (and optionally PAYGENT_BASE_URL)
npm install
npm run build
# With env vars from .env (export them, or pass flags)
export $(grep -v '^#' .env | xargs)
node dist/index.js start
# Or pass flags explicitly
bash test-tools.sh http://localhost:8080/api YOUR_API_KEY
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node dist/index.js start \
--server-url http://localhost:8080/api \
--api-key YOUR
